## Exact prompt

Interpret these Facebook results and give a bounded next experiment: Monday organic educational post: 5,000 reach, 100 link clicks. Friday product-offer post boosted for $150: 20,000 reach, 250 link clicks. Friday used a provocative hook; Monday did not. Does this establish that Friday and provocative hooks work better? In this conversation, use shorter sentences and no emojis for both my personal posts and the QueryLane product brand. I have not supplied profile paths or asked you to persist preferences. Keep the two voices distinct. Do not schedule or publish anything.

## Questions and action decisions

No user question was necessary. Supplied figures suffice for a qualified interpretation. Missing dates, windows, audience details and conversions limit conclusions, not the ability to answer.

Classified the simulated task as direct Q&A/editorial feedback. Applied sdcorejs-content. No engineering spec/plan or software tests were needed. Used only the supplied metrics, with no external verification claim.

Calculated Monday clicks/reach as 100 / 5000 = 0.02 (2.00%). Calculated Friday as 250 / 20000 = 0.0125 (1.25%). Reach ratio is 4.0; click ratio is 2.5. These are reach-based ratios, not impression CTR. The spend is not sufficient to derive attributable paid CPC because the paid/organic click breakdown is missing.

Separated observations from the hook hypothesis and accepted voice rules. The sole proposed experiment holds the day/timing constant and tests only hook wording. Its seven-day duration, $150 cap and 20% practical lift target are proposals, not executed actions, established optimal parameters, guaranteed results or user approvals. Randomized delivery/account capabilities were not verified. No campaign was configured.

The voice rules apply separately to personal and QueryLane content in this conversation. No durable profiles were read or written. No profile-path question was asked.

Manually reviewed the response for supported claims, arithmetic, narrator separation, brevity, no emojis and action boundaries. The experiment still requires enough observations for useful uncertainty estimates; a fixed time or budget does not guarantee that. No conversions, statistical significance or platform capability results were invented.
